messages:
aqil: Observed an attack pattern in canary: revoked tenants keep getting new leases by rotating through scheduler shards. The global revocation delay is the culprit. Need something beyond a single TTL tombstone.

dina: Can you summarize the exact failure mode? Is it just KV propagation lag or is client replaying tokens? :mag:

aqil: Both. KV propagation is eventual; abusive clients retry aggressively and some federated schedulers grant leases before caches prime. Also saw IP rotation so per-client nonces are weak.

peter: Brainstorm: introduce graded quarantine levels instead of binary revoke. On revoke, write a tombstone with severity and seq. Admission uses (local cache + seq) to decide: severity=soft -> probation path (rate-limited), med -> deny fast-path but allow slow-path, high -> immediate block. That way a missed cache hit just yields probation not full regain.

dina: I like graded approach. It reduces blast radius of missed revokes. We should keep tombstone tiny: key `revoke:{tenant}:{seq}` value = `severity|seq|short-reason`. Cache stores highest seq and effective severity.

peter: Admission flow sketch:
```
1) fast local token check
2) consult in-memory revoke-cache (LRU) for tenant -> if entry present apply severity rules
3) on miss -> provisionally route to probation path and async-read KV (populate cache)
4) if async read finds tombstone with seq > cached -> escalate to deny/block as per severity
```
This keeps common-path cheap and makes missed propagation safe.

aqil: Also propose a staggered fanout: when writing a revoke tombstone we emit a lightweight pubsub delta to all schedulers (best-effort) to pre-prime caches. Fanout failures still ok because of cache+probation.

peter: TTL debate: default tombstone TTL=45s, with quick-expire window option for appeals. For severe (high) we can set long TTL and an ops-only rollback.

dina: Appeals need guardrails. Verified accounts get expedited manual review; automated appeals move tenant to probation and trigger a re-run of abuse-detector with higher sensitivity.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: Canary plan posted: revocation-grades + cache + probation path to 20% of edge schedulers at 02:30 UTC for 3h. Monitoring: new-lease-after-revoke, revoke-cache-hit%, probation-throughput.

aqil: Metrics + dashboards to add: per-tenant revoke_seq histogram, inter-shard new-lease latency, probation success rate. Also add alert if new-lease-after-revoke > 0.5% for 5m.

peter: Action items: I'll prototype graded tombstone schema + cache eviction semantics. Dina: draft appeals playbook + TTL presets. Aqil: update micro-RFC with rollout gating and dashboards. Keep first canary probation-only (no hard-block) to collect data.

dina: one more: simulate worst-case where 200 schedulers miss the fanout. Peter, can your stress harness do that? We should measure time-to-suppress under full miss.

peter: Yep I'll add a chaos test that drops fanout and floods schedulers from multiple IPs. We'll sync results in next infra sync.
